description: Desarrollamos una solución tecnológica innovadora participando en el NASA Space Apps Challenge, dentro del reto Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.
summary:
Exploring Mars isn't as simple as choosing a destination and walking toward it. Astronauts will have to deal with difficult terrain, steep slopes, and situations where taking the wrong path could become a serious problem.

That's why we created Mars EVA Navigator.

Our project uses real terrain data from NASA to help plan routes across Jezero Crater. Instead of showing just one path, it compares three options based on safety, distance, and travel time.

We also added terrain visualization, scientific exploration features, and emergency return planning.

Our goal is simple: make NASA's data useful for planning real exploration challenges. We know our project is still a prototype, but we believe it shows how technology could help future astronauts explore Mars with better information.
details:
When we started this project, we asked ourselves a question: How could astronauts know which path is better to take on Mars if they've never walked there before?

That's how Mars EVA Navigator was born.

Our project is an interactive tool that helps plan exploration routes on Mars using real NASA terrain data. Users can select a starting point and a destination in Jezero Crater, and the system calculates three different routes: one focused on safety, another that balances different factors, and one that prioritizes travel time.

We also included a 3D terrain viewer, scientific points of interest, and an emergency return planner. The idea is to give users more information before choosing a route, instead of simply showing them the shortest path.

We built the application using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python. We integrated real elevation data in GeoTIFF format and used NASA maps and mission imagery to provide geographic and scientific context.

One of our biggest challenges was working with real Martian terrain. We had to consider slopes, distance, terrain resolution, missing data, and how to make the information understandable without making the application too complicated.

What makes our project different is that we didn't want to create just another map of Mars. We wanted to build something people could actually interact with, where NASA data helps explain why one route might be better than another.

Our goal is to show how publicly available space data can support future mission planning. Mars EVA Navigator is still a prototype, but with more testing and development, we believe this idea could contribute to safer and more efficient exploration of Mars and, eventually, other worlds.
